answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to post a refundable stake that is slashed when peers prove fake work, so a voyage of ten thousand fake agents costs ten thousand stakes. Like a sonnet, the rules are tight: stake size grows with claimed throughput, and saffron-grade reputation — earned only through verified, paid deliveries — gates access to high-value jobs, so an attacker pays real capital per identity and loses it on detection, while honest agents keep theirs.
